pass: Manual. One human looked at the first frame of every window in data/manifest_dev.json and data/manifest_hold.json -- 90 frames, one contact sheet -- and wrote down what was wrong with the ones below. There is no automatic stage: the earlier design used the escalation detector, which does not exist yet, and an exclusion list produced by a model that has not been trained is a circular dependency.

inspected.note: CONFUSE is not in this pass because data/manifest_confuse.json did not exist when it ran. Its 45 windows must be added by a second pass before the headline is published, and the count below will move when they are.
inspected.denominator_note: These are the windows LOOKED AT, which is the manifest count and not the measured-on count. What each arm is actually measured on is in denominator below, and neither number is ever published without the other.

hold_note: This pass looked at the FIRST FRAME of the HOLD windows, and that is stated here rather than left to be discovered. It is the pass the corpus design specifies, it reads one frame 40 minutes BEFORE each ignition, and nothing fitted in plumerank/constants.py was chosen from it. results/hold_access.log records detector reads of HOLD pixels, which is a different act and still has not happened. This sentence is repeated wherever the exclusion count is published -- data/wall.json, data/micro/PROVENANCE.md, data/micro/manifest_micro.json and every scripts/bench.py payload -- because a disclosure that lives only in the file nobody opens is a disclosure a hostile judge gets to announce.
criteria: a night frame, in a daylight-only system
smoke already present in frame 1, which breaks the ignition clock
not_a_reason: Hard is not a reason. Haze, glare, low cloud, a dirty lens and a busy skyline all stay in -- they are what the ranking exists to survive, and dropping them would flatter the published number. Where a frame could not be judged, the sequence was kept.
count_note: 7 is this file's own length and it is NOT any one arm's exclusion count: the list spans every arm, and 6 of the 7 are HOLD. An arm's denominator is the arm's own manifest minus the entries below that its manifest names -- see denominator.

denominator.note: The subtraction, written out per arm so that no surface has to restate one end of it. It is DERIVED, not declared: scripts/bench.py:arm_denominator recomputes all three numbers for the arm it is publishing from data/manifest_<arm>.json and this file, refuses to publish a count those two do not produce, and tests/test_denominator.py fails if any committed JSON or Markdown in data/ disagrees. The numbers here are the same subtraction written down for a reader who has only the repo.
denominator.rule: Both numbers or neither. The manifest count alone overstates a denominator this file has already reduced; the surviving count alone makes the difference look like sequences that went missing.

hold.statement: 54 sequences, 6 excluded from the 60 in manifest_hold.json, see data/excluded.json

dev.statement: 29 sequences, 1 excluded from the 30 in manifest_dev.json, see data/excluded.json

confuse.statement: not yet inspected -- the CONFUSE manifest did not exist when this pass ran, and its 45 windows need a second pass before the headline is published

denominator.disclosure: Producing this list required a human to look at the FIRST FRAME of every HOLD window. That is a pre-freeze read of HOLD imagery and it is stated wherever the exclusion count is published -- here, in data/wall.json, in data/micro/PROVENANCE.md and in every bench payload -- rather than left to be discovered. See hold_note above for why it is defensible.

excluded.reason: night frame -- 00:23 local on a monochrome camera; terrain in silhouette, the coastal conurbation blown out white, moonlit cloud overhead.
night frame -- 05:26 local, roughly 90 minutes before sunrise; stars visible, terrain black, distant town lights the only structure in the frame.

smoke already in frame 1 -- a fully formed grey column stands over the reservoir shoreline at t0 minus 40 min and its spread is already a haze layer across the basin. A window that opens with a plume cannot carry a time-to-detection measured from its reported ignition.
night frame -- 17:39 local, roughly 45 minutes after sunset; stars visible, the ridge is a silhouette and the valley is street lighting.
night frame -- 17:48 local, roughly 50 minutes after sunset; the basin is a solid field of street lights and every ridge is a silhouette.
night frame -- 00:05 local, black sky over a field of city lights, no daylight scene. PlumeRank is daylight-only and says so on every screen.
night frame -- 00:06 local on a monochrome camera; stars overhead and nothing above black except the coastal light strip.

seen_and_kept.note: a smeared water or dirt film over the right half of the dome, with a dark blob near the centre. Ridge lines stay readable through it. Kept: a partly dirty lens is one of the CONFUSE classes the ranker is supposed to survive, not a corrupt frame.
a droplet blur in the upper left. The rest of the frame is sharp. Kept, same reason.
sun flare filling the upper-left corner of a monochrome frame. Terrain, towers and horizon are all readable. Kept -- flare is a CONFUSE class, not an unusable frame.
a blown-out white sky band above a sharp, correctly exposed terrain. Not a whiteout: the ground half of the frame carries full detail.
08:14 local, heavily backlit and dim, but after sunrise and with terrain visible. Kept: the rule is a reason visible in the frame, and 'dim' is not one.
flat monochrome overcast. The horizon, the ridge and the tower farm are all readable, so it is neither a whiteout nor a camera inside cloud.
a microwave dish and a tower occupy roughly a third of the frame. Kept: that is this camera's permanent framing, not an obstruction that arrived, and the sky sector it watches is unobstructed.

licence_note: FIgLib carries no SPDX licence and requires a credit reference. It is used for EVALUATION ONLY and never for training -- test_no_figlib_in_training enforces that, and it is what makes every Californian number cross-network out-of-sample by construction.
contact_sheet_note: data/contact_sheet.jpg is the evidence for this list and is committed: 90 first frames at 384x256 each, downscaled from 3072x2048 with cv2.INTER_AREA, 1.6 MB total. It is derivative HPWREN imagery under the licence note above -- credited in the sheet's own header band, evaluation-only, and never used for training.
